ety.text: Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰengʰ-der. Proto-Germanic *ganganą Proto-West Germanic *gangan Old English gangan Middle English gangen English gang From Middle English gangen, from Old English gangan (“to go, walk, turn out”), from Proto-West Germanic *gangan, from Proto-Germanic *ganganą (“to go, walk”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰengʰ- (“to step, walk”). Cognate with Scots gang (“to go on foot, walk”), Swedish gånga (“to walk, go”), Faroese ganga (“to walk”), Icelandic ganga (“to walk, go”), Norwegian Nynorsk ganga (“to walk, go”), Vedic Sanskrit जंहस् (jáṃhas).

From Middle English gang, from Old English gang (“a journey; way; passage”), from Proto-West Germanic *gang, from Proto-Germanic *gangaz, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰongʰ-o-s, from *ǵʰengʰ- (“to step; stride”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian Gong, Dutch gang, German Gang, Norwegian gang, Swedish gång, Icelandic gangur, Vedic Sanskrit जंहस् (jáṃhas).
Shortening of gangbang.

senses.d: A number going in company; a number of friends or persons associated for a particular purpose.
ex: The gang from our office is going out for drinks Friday night.

senses.d: A group of laborers under one foreman; a squad or workgang.
ex: a gang of sailors; a railroad gang; a labor gang or pool.

senses.d: A criminal group with a common cultural background and identifying features, often associated with a particular section of a city.
ex: a youth gang; a neighborhood gang; motorcycle gang.

senses.d: A group of criminals or alleged criminals who band together for mutual protection and profit.
ex: The Winter Hill Gang was quite proficient at murdering rival mobsters in order to take over their rackets.

senses.d: A group of politicians united in furtherance of a political goal.
ex: The Gang of Four was led by Jiang Qing, the fourth wife of Mao Zedong.
Not all members of the Gang of Six are consistent in their opposition to filibuster.

senses.d: A term of address for a group, particularly when cautioning them or offering advice.
A term of address for any other person or group of people.
ex: The sun isn't real? What are you even talking about, gang?
One day they followed a gang of deer that ran in toward the settlements.
saw Several gangs of Elk on each Side of the river. late in the afternoon we Saw a gang of Buffaloe
Nearly every farmer has a "gang" of turkeys.
On our way back to the camp the dogs run into a gang of turkeys.

senses.d: To attach similar items together to form a larger unit.
ex: Volume controls may be ganged to mode switches to provide maximum output […]
When cutting the back cleats with the T-guide, first gang them together so all the marks on one side align.
He still liked the idea of them all ganging her [...]
